- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply +1–2% bias to first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15-day moving average of past 30 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or volatile (0.00–0.33), model often lags; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend, but not exceed 3% above recent high.
